chapter: Later years: recordings, Alice and the book
title: The 1999 Tribeca interview and Living Time Orchestra concerts
summary: Daughtry recalls the live interview in Manhattan, the first New York concert in 20 years, and the Library of Congress concert; Alice names band members.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I was saying that I had the pleasure of meeting you, after talking to you on the phone for several years, at Tribeca, Manhattan Borough College, down in lower Manhattan, where you – where we did a live interview, first of all, in front of a couple hundred people, which was wonderful and very enlightening and stimulating for me. In addition to that, it was a historic concert that your International Living Time Orchestra performed later that evening. It was the first time that you had appeared in New York in 20 years. There was a tremendous level of excitement. I know, because I was there. I talked to people. There were – there may have been hundreds. I know for a fact that there were dozens, because I saw about 20 to 30 that I personally knew.
Was that the Living Time Orchestra?

Yes, and there were dozens of musicians who not only came to the interview, because they were anxious to hear you talk about your Concept, which you did, and you demonstrated on a piano. It was absolutely superb. I loved it. And then the concert, which was fantastic, two nights later. Again, courtesy, or as part of the [?McKem] Fund commission for the Library of Congress, you performed at the Library of Congress auditorium, one of their music halls – Coolidge, I believe it is – in a sold-out, packed concert that was tremendously well received. Again you had your International Living Time Orchestra. Fantastic.
Yeah. This was the music of the people.

We danced. We were moving out there in the audience. The great thing about that hall, there’s not a bad sightline anywhere. I have said any number of times over the course of these four tapes, the International Living Time Orchestra – your musicians are from all over, aren’t they?
And the States. It’s half and half. It’s American, half British, with the occasional melancholy Dane, who’s Palle Mikkelborg on trumpet.
Right. Andy Shepherd, the wonderful saxophonist from London
